subject: Re: Stratus.ai security questionnaire — hosted API data residency & retention
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@stratus.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: 2027-06-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Stratus security questionnaire — hosted API residency + retention

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the time to respond to our security questionnaire. Attached is the current version (Stratus_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf). We have a couple of sections we need clarified quickly for our internal compliance review:

1) Data residency: Can Redwood guarantee that customer data for our account will remain within a US region? We need confirmation that backups, logs, and any maintenance snapshots will not leave the requested geography.

2) Retention & deletion: We are looking for the exact retention windows for (a) request logs, (b) user-provided payloads (input/output), and (c) model cache artifacts (KV cache). Please also outline the deletion workflow when a customer requests complete erasure.

3) Cross-region failover: If you offer cross-region fallbacks, what is the maximum replication window and do you encrypt those transfers?

Would appreciate a short Q&A summary we can attach to the questionnaire. We are on a tight procurement timeline — ideally by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Elena Park\Security & Compliance, Stratus.ai

Attachment: Stratus_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@stratus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus security questionnaire — hosted API residency + retention

Elena,

Thanks — we can get this into a concise Q&A for you. Below are the short answers up front; I put more context and explicit workflow steps after.

1) Data residency: Yes — for Hosted API customers we bind data to a selected geography at the account level. If you choose US-only, production requests, logs, backups, and routine snapshots are stored in the selected US region(s) only. We do not replicate customer data to other regions unless you opt-in to cross-region failover.

2) Retention & deletion:
  - Request logs (ingestion metadata, timestamps, routing): retained 90 days by default; configurable down to 30 days on request.
  - Payloads (input/output content): ephemeral by default; retained for 30 days for debugging and billing purposes unless you elect shorter retention.
  - Model KV cache artifacts: cached in-memory and persisted only when necessary for warm-starts; persisted caches are retained for 7 days and are not included in long-term backups.
  - Deletion workflow: a customer erasure request triggers: (a) account flag -> immediate stop of new data retention; (b) asynchronous purge of persisted payloads and logs per region (within SLA window); (c) verification job that confirms deletion and writes an audit event. Typical completion: 48–72 hours for hosted accounts, dependent on data volume.

3) Cross-region failover:
  - Off by default. If enabled, replication is asynchronous with a typical RPO of up to 30 minutes for active routing tables. All transfer traffic is TLS 1.3 and uses AES-256 in transit. Replicated snapshots are encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys (optional).

Detailed notes (for your questionnaire doc):
- Backups & snapshots: Redwood takes incremental snapshots for operational recovery. For US-only customers these snapshots are stored in the same US region block and encrypted with service-side keys by default. We can offer CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for Dedicated/Private plans; Hosted customers can request CMEK under an enterprise addendum.
- Logs & telemetry: Operational logs required for rate limits, billing, and security are scoped to the account and kept in-region. Aggregated system telemetry (anonymized) may be used for platform improvements; raw account-linked logs stay in-region.
- Deletion attestations: After an erasure request we can provide a signed deletion confirmation and the internal audit job id. If you need a certificate-style attestation, we can route a formal SOC-2 attestation request through our CSP.
- Edge-case: snapshots taken for platform upgrades are short-lived (under 72 hours) and are automatically cleaned; they are stored in-region and encrypted.

I attached a lightweight data flow diagram and a one-page Q&A you can paste into the questionnaire. Karthik and Soojin are copied for any technical follow-up.

Jonas Weber\Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png; Redwood_QA_onepager.pdf (summary)

From: Stratus Security Team <security@stratus.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@stratus.ai>, procurement@stratus.ai
Date: 2027-06-21T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus security questionnaire — hosted API residency + retention

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick summary — that helps. Two follow-ups before we finalize:

A) For payloads retained for 30 days: are those encrypted at rest with keys separated per customer? Can Redwood guarantee those payloads are not used for training models or improving underlying models?

B) For the deletion workflow: does your verification job remove entries from backups as well or only from live stores? In particular, if a snapshot includes a customer's persisted cache, how is that handled?

Also, can you confirm whether audit logs that are kept for security review include any customer plaintext payloads, or are they metadata-only?

Regards,
Stratus Security Team

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Stratus Security Team <security@stratus.ai>, Elena Park <elena@stratus.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-22T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus security questionnaire — hosted API residency + retention

Hi Elena / Security Team,

Appreciate the thoughtful questions — below are precise answers you can paste back into the questionnaire.

A) Encryption & training usage:
  - At rest: Customer payloads stored in-region are encrypted at rest using AES-256. For Hosted plans encryption is service-managed by default; we can enable customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for enterprise agreements. Keys are scoped per tenant in the KMS and access is restricted via IAM.
  - Use for training: Redwood does NOT use customer plaintext payloads to train our foundation models. We have a strict data usage policy documented in our DPA: customer data submitted to hosted inference endpoints will not be incorporated into model training unless the customer explicitly opts in via a separate agreement.

B) Deletion & backups:
  - Live stores: The erasure job removes persisted payloads, logs, and cache artifacts from live stores and updates the account state.
  - Backups/snapshots: Incremental backups that include customer data are pruned on the next backup cycle after an erasure request; for most hosted accounts that means the offending data is removed from recoverable backups within the SLA window (typically 72 hours). For governance we retain an internal deletion audit trail (no customer plaintext) to prove the delete event occurred.
  - Cache artifacts in snapshots: Persisted KV caches are intentionally small and are excluded from long-term archival; if they appear in a short-lived snapshot they are removed via the same purge process and not retained beyond the stated window.

C) Audit logs: Security/audit logs aimed at incident investigation contain metadata (request ids, timestamps, source IPs, model version). We do not include full customer plaintext in standard audit exports. If your team requires a hardened audit with additional fields we can discuss a scoped export under an NDA.

Next steps: I attached the redwood-data-flow-diagram.png and a short Q&A text file that directly maps to your questionnaire sections. If you want a signed deletion attestation and a one-off copy of the DPA with the hosting addendum, send procurement@redwood.ai an order reference and we’ll route it.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer\Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png; Redwood_Data_Residency_QA.txt
